name: Melrose
headline: Three train stops, one pond in the middle,
and Victorian streets that lead to the Fells.
answer: Melrose is a Middlesex County city of 29,817 people (2020 Census), about seven miles north of Boston. More than half its homes predate World War II, many Victorian near downtown and the rail line. Three MBTA Haverhill Line stations serve the city, and Oak Grove on the Orange Line sits just over the Malden border.
overview: Melrose was part of Charlestown and then Malden before it was incorporated as a town in 1850. When the Boston and Maine Railroad built three stops through it in 1845, houses followed the tracks, and in 1853 the town annexed the highlands from Stoneham. Melrose became a city in 1900. Its downtown, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1982, runs along Main Street, and Ell Pond, the city's largest body of water, sits near the center with a gazebo and a new fountain.

The housing tells the city's history in layers. A 2022 housing plan found that most homes built before World War II cluster near downtown and the rail corridor, often in Victorian styles, while the eastern side filled in after the war with ranches and Capes. Larger buildings are concentrated downtown and along Main Street. At the edges are big green spaces: the eastern reaches of the Middlesex Fells, the Olmsted-designed Pine Banks Park on the Malden line, and Mount Hood, a city park and golf course with views toward Boston.

Melrose meets the state's MBTA Communities law, as a commuter rail community, through zoning it already had: the Rail Corridor Overlay District, the Smart Growth Overlay District, the Urban Residential-D district and the Medical Business district, with a few minor amendments. The state lists it as compliant, as of October 21, 2026. Since 2004 the city's Affordable Housing Incentive Program ordinance has required certain residential and mixed-use projects to set aside 15 percent of their units as affordable to households earning up to 80 percent of the Boston-area median income. The city's affordable housing office lists such units in projects including the Windsor Radio Factory at 99 Washington Street (19 rentals, offered by lottery in 2022), The Washingtons at 2 and 37/47 Washington Street (17 rentals, 2015 and 2016) and Jack Flats at 1000 Stone Place (19 rentals, 2013 and 2014).

housing.text: Melrose's 2022 Housing Production Plan reports that 55% of homes are detached single-family and 11% are two-family, with 16% in buildings of 20 or more units. Over half were built before World War II, often in Victorian styles near downtown and the rail corridor; the eastern parts of the city saw more mid-century ranch and Cape houses after the war.

villages.name: Downtown Melrose
villages.line: The Main Street business district, listed on the National Register in 1982, where most buildings of five or more units are found.

villages.name: Melrose Highlands
villages.line: The northern section annexed from Stoneham in 1853, served by its own Haverhill Line station.

villages.name: Cedar Park
villages.line: A neighborhood along the rail corridor around the Melrose/Cedar Park station.

villages.name: Wyoming
villages.line: The southern neighborhood around Wyoming Hill station, closest to Malden.

villages.name: East Side
villages.line: The eastern part of the city, built up mostly after World War II with ranch and Cape houses.

villages.name: Oak Grove and Pine Banks
villages.line: The southern edge near the Malden line, next to Pine Banks Park and the Oak Grove station.

rail.line: Orange Line (subway, in Malden near the Melrose border)

commute.text: Three Haverhill Line stations run to Boston's North Station, and Oak Grove, the Orange Line terminal, is just over the line in Malden. Only a short stretch of Route 99 lies within the city; I-93 is reached in Stoneham, Route 1 in Saugus and I-95/Route 128 in Wakefield.

places.name: Middlesex Fells Reservation
places.line: A DCR reservation with more than 100 miles of trails, whose eastern reaches extend into Melrose.

places.name: Ell Pond Park
places.line: The city's largest pond, near the center, with a gazebo and a fountain that helps keep the water healthy.

places.name: Pine Banks Park
places.line: A 107.5-acre park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and shared with Malden, with cliffs, a pond, fields and a playground.

places.name: Mount Hood Park and Golf Course
places.line: A wooded city park of about 300 acres with an 18-hole course built under the WPA and winter sledding.

places.name: Downtown Melrose
places.line: A Main Street district on the National Register of Historic Places since 1982.

places.name: Melrose Public Library
places.line: A 1904 Colonial Revival building by the Lynn architect Penn Varney at 69 West Emerson Street, listed on the National Register on June 23, 1988.

places.name: Swains Pond and Towners Pond
places.line: East-side ponds near Mount Hood whose surrounding land is part of the greenbelt, which the city says makes up 26 percent of its land.

history.text: The Boston and Maine Railroad built three stops through the town, today's Wyoming Hill, Melrose/Cedar Park and Melrose Highlands stations.
Incorporated as the Town of Melrose, having been part of Charlestown and then Malden.
Annexed the highlands from neighboring Stoneham, setting today's borders.
Became a city, the 33rd in Massachusetts, with Levi S. Gould as first mayor.

search_notes: 'Melrose MA real estate agent' returns agent-matching and review directories (HomeLight, BiggerPockets, Experience.com), Bean Group and Redfin listings, with no strong local-guide content. 'Moving to Melrose MA' is almost entirely moving companies (All My Sons, Gentle Giant, HireAHelper, Lugg, MoveBuddha) plus Livability. A guide that explains the three train stops, the Victorian-to-postwar housing pattern and the parks would fill a clear gap.

faq.q: What is the median home price in Melrose, MA?
faq.a: According to The Warren Group's MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town table, the median single-family sale price in Melrose for calendar year 2025 was $965,000, across 187 sales. In 2024 it was $869,000, across 191 sales.
Yes. Melrose has three MBTA Haverhill Line stations: Melrose Highlands, Melrose/Cedar Park and Wyoming Hill. Oak Grove, on the Orange Line, is just across the border in Malden.
Melrose Public Schools. Review its profile with DESE.

faq.q: What is the property tax rate in Melrose?
faq.a: For fiscal year 2026, the City of Melrose Assessor lists a residential rate of $11.47 per $1,000 of assessed value and a commercial, industrial and personal property rate of $20.61.

faq.q: How does Melrose comply with the MBTA Communities law?
faq.a: Through existing zoning: the Rail Corridor Overlay, Smart Growth Overlay, Urban Residential-D and Medical Business districts, with minor amendments. The state lists Melrose as compliant as of October 21, 2026.

notes: Condo figures set to null: the PDF's extracted text ends partway through the condo table (at Brookline), so Melrose's condo rows could not be read. Wikipedia gives both 1628 and 1629 as the settlement date, so neither is used. Neighborhood lines for Cedar Park, Wyoming and Oak Grove/Pine Banks are inferred from station and park locations named on Wikipedia, not from a dedicated neighborhood source. The Ell Pond source is the city Park Department page on the CivicPlus host (ma-melrose.civicplus.com), which serves the same site as cityofmelrose.org. Deepened 2026-10-22: added a third overview paragraph on zoning and affordable housing (sources: the city's MBTA Communities Law page, https://www.cityofmelrose.org/783/MBTA-Communities-Law, for the category and the four districts; the state list at https://www.mass.gov/doc/mbta-communities-district-compliance-letters/download, 'As of October 21, 2026', no. 79 Melrose; the city's Affordable Housing page, https://www.cityofmelrose.org/370/Affordable-Housing, for the 2004 ordinance, the 15 percent requirement and the projects). The city page does not give the council vote date, the compliance determination date or the districts' unit capacity; the project unit counts are the affordable units listed by the city, not total units. The 2022 HPP PDF could not be reread this session (binary data), so the existing housing text is kept unchanged. Removed the 'Mount Hood' village entry to bring villages to six; Mount Hood remains under places and the East Side entry. Places added: Melrose Public Library (Wikipedia) and Swains Pond and Towners Pond (Wikipedia, Melrose, for their location; city Trails & Open Areas page for the greenbelt). History added: 1845 railroad stops (Wikipedia). Tax object and FAQ from the Assessor page; the FY2025 rate is from https://ma-melrose.civicplus.com/DocumentCenter/View/2824/FY2026-Property-Tax-Classification; the state's FY2026 tax-rate summary (https://www.mass.gov/info-details/fy2026-tax-levies-assessed-values-and-tax-rates) notes Melrose had the largest dollar increase in a commercial rate from FY2025 ($2.86).
